reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is verifying AI-generated content against probabilistic guarantees without access to ground truth outcomes. Conformal prediction provides a frequentist solution by constructing prediction sets that contain the true outcome with prescribed probability, regardless of model complexity. The "thin evidence" scenario translates directly into a hypothesis test about the informativeness of the evidence set. When evidence is sparse, the resulting prediction intervals become wide, signaling refusal. This bridges to GSI's Bayesian framework via duality between conformal sets and credible intervals under certain priors. The situational automaton then discretizes these continuous probabilistic decisions into hard refusal actions, creating a cascading verification pipeline.
